## OmniRoute v3.8.54

- **Providers:** official "Sign in with ChatGPT" provider (`chatgpt`, PKCE + live model discovery); MiniMax Code (managed gateway + dashboard device-code sign-in); RenderHour (images, video, speech); MegaBrain (dual auth); EmpirioLabs, ParalonCloud, deAPI, Replicate chat, Cerebrium, Hetzner Inference and Grokified; native `opencode-server` executor; Microsoft 365 Copilot work/school sign-in; GitHub Copilot embeddings; Gemini Lyria 3 music models; custom JSON API provider nodes (request template + response path).
- **Routing and combos:** endpoint-specific combo routes (chat, search/fetch, embeddings, rerank, images, video, music, OCR, audio) with capability-aware search/fetch combos; new `jev` and `expiry-first` strategies; preferred and reserve accounts for Auto combos; opt-in preferred-account response-start failover; opt-in deadline-failure sub-budget that ends a combo with a clean 504.
- **Search:** Keenable web search and fetch provider (keyless by default) and `codex-search` through connected Codex accounts.
- **API keys and usage:** `/v1/me/status` reports today's/this week's usage and every per-key limit; `/v1/me/sessions` self-service session listing; rolling 5-hour USD budget per key; reusable key policy templates; `POST /api/keys/import`; usage attributed to coding-agent sessions and projects; provider-reported cache-read and 5-minute/1-hour cache-write tiers carried through analytics.
- **Agentic pipelines and streaming:** repeated-tool-round and consecutive-failure detection across native protocols; opt-in context compaction with per-model budgets; `STREAM_READINESS_TIMEOUT` now says which failure shape occurred; large request bodies to `api.anthropic.com` are gzip-compressed like Claude Code.
- **Privacy and media:** opt-in reversible PII token vault (default off, requires `PII_REDACTION_ENABLED`); consented, tenant-bound Video Bridge frame drill-down handles with dashboard controls; opt-in image normalization before dispatch.
- **Dashboard:** "New models" inbox across connected providers; Costs > Pricing model comparison across providers and a "Configured only" filter; Quota Tracker order synced across browsers; Cmd+K ranked by match quality; Codex personal plan vs Business seat; "Quota check" toggle for compatible nodes.
- **Distribution and release engineering:** Docker images also published to the Cheaper Inference organization (`cheaperinference/omniroute`) and GHCR, Electron auto-update served from `cheaper-inference/OmniRoute`; derived counts refreshed only at release (`npm run facts`, `release:refresh-derived`); timestamped migration names; the omni-queue merge queue (shadow mode); complete European Portuguese (PT-PT) catalog and the 66 locales synced at release.

## Combos: the flagship 1. **Start with `auto`.** Set the model in your OpenAI-compatible client. OmniRoute builds a virtual combo from connected providers and scores candidates live. 2. **Save a combo for more control.** Choose a name, target list and strategy, then use that name as the model. The strategy sets which target goes first and how the rest are tried. A combo routes across models automatically. On quota exhaustion, provider failure or model lockout, it tries the next eligible, healthy target. ### Zero-config: just use `auto` ```bash curl http://localhost:20128/v1/chat/completions \ -H "Authorization: Bearer " \ -H "Content-Type: application/json" \ -d '{"model": "auto", "messages": [{"role": "user", "content": "Hello"}]}' ``` Variants tune the weights. Last-known-good routing stays with the last successful provider until it fails, then rescores. `auto/fast` and `auto/cheap` express preferences without guaranteeing the fastest or cheapest model. | Model ID | Behavior | | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `auto` | Balanced default weights. | | `auto/fast` | Favors low latency and provider health. | | `auto/cheap` | Favors lower catalog prices. | | `auto/coding` | Quality-first weights for code generation. | | `auto/smart` | Quality-first weights with 10% exploration (default 5%). | | `auto/lkgp` | Explicit last-known-good routing with the same weights as `auto`. | | `auto/subscription` | Uses only live-verified plan quota. Returns HTTP 503 when none is available and avoids billed fallback. | | `auto/thrifty` | Plan → keyless → free → cheap → premium. May reach billed models and returns to the plan when quota and cooldown allow. | | `auto/offline` | Favors quota and rate-limit headroom. Requests still go to your providers. | | `auto/chaos` | One model per provider in parallel, up to five by default or ten when configured. One upstream call per model. Returns the top-ranked reply or the last successful panel reply if the top model fails. Use `fusion` to synthesize replies with a judge. | Category and optional tier examples include `auto/coding:fast`, `auto/coding:free`, `auto/reasoning:pro` and `auto/vision`. If no connected candidate matches, the request returns HTTP 503 and the pool stays narrow. [Auto-Combo guide](./docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md) · [Subscription-first routing](./docs/routing/SUBSCRIPTION_LADDER.md) ### Or build your own: 22 routing strategies ```bash omniroute combo create my-pool --strategy fill-first \ --models "provider-a/model-1,provider-b/model-2" ``` The CLI accepts 15 of 22 strategies. The dashboard and combos API accept all 22. | Strategy | Behavior | | :------------------ | :------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------ | | `auto` | Rank candidates live with the 16-factor Auto-Combo scorer. | | `cache-optimized` | Prefer the account likely to hold the prompt prefix in cache. | | `context-optimized` | Try the largest known context window first. | | `context-relay` | Keep your order and pass a conversation summary when switching accounts. | | `cost-optimized` | Sort by catalog input-token price, unknowns last. Final request cost can differ. | | `expiry-first` | Spend quota likely to expire, highest leftover per hour until reset first. | | `fill-first` | Stay on the first available target until it runs out or fails, then move on. | | `fusion` | Query a panel in parallel and have a judge synthesize one answer. | | `headroom` | Choose the most free capacity across 5-hour and weekly windows. | | `jev` | TypeSafe Jev picks which entries in your ranked list run. Turn on `COMBO_JEV_STRATEGY_ENABLED` to send an excerpt per request and use paid TypeSafe calls. With it off, your order applies. | | `least-used` | Pick the target with the fewest recorded requests in this combo. | | `lkgp` | Try the last successful provider first, otherwise keep your order. | | `p2c` | Sample two targets and pick by success rate and latency. | | `pipeline` | Feed each step's output into the next target in sequence and return only the final answer. | | `priority` | Try targets in your order. Session stickiness preserves it. | | `quota-weighted` | Skip exhausted accounts and draw by leftover quota and in-flight load. | | `random` | Shuffle for each request. The same first target can repeat. | | `reset-aware` | Score remaining quota and time to reset across session and weekly windows. | | `reset-window` | Try the account whose quota window resets soonest. | | `round-robin` | Rotate in order, three successes per target by default. | | `strict-random` | Deal from a shuffled deck so each target leads once before repeats. | | `weighted` | Draw a first target by weight and keep the rest as fallbacks. The split is statistical. Use `round-robin` for strict rotation. | Quota strategies use live data where providers report it, including 5-hour and weekly subscription windows. `fusion` and `pipeline` make multiple upstream calls per request. The 16-factor scorer uses quota, health, cost, latency, task fit, stability, tier priority, tier affinity, specificity match, context affinity, cache affinity, session availability, reset-window affinity, connection density, quality and reliability. Weights vary by profile. Cache affinity, reset-window affinity and reliability have zero weight by default. [Scoring factors](./docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md#how-it-works-persisted-auto-combos) In a saved combo with `strategy: "auto"`, `config.routerStrategy` selects `rules`, `score`, `cost` (`eco`), `latency` (`fast`), `sla-aware` (`sla`), `lkgp`, `nadir` or `decision`. [Auto router strategies](./docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md#auto-router-strategies) ### Resilience is built in: 3 independent layers Failures are handled at three scopes, so one bad model does not take down its account, and one bad account does not take down its provider. #### If a whole provider is down The **provider circuit breaker** opens after 8 (OAuth) or 12 (API key) failures with status 408, 500, 502, 503 or 504. Combos skip that provider while it is open. After 60 s or 30 s, one probe request decides whether it closes. #### If one key or account is rate-limited The **connection cooldown** benches only that connection, with exponential backoff from 5 s (OAuth) or 3 s (API key). Other keys for the same provider keep serving. #### If one model is refused The **model lockout** blocks only that model on that connection after a per-model 429, 404 or access denial. Other models on the same connection keep serving. Banned, expired and out-of-credit connections are terminal states, not cooldowns: they wait for you to fix them. [Auto-Combo engine](docs/routing/AUTO-COMBO.md) · [Resilience guide](docs/architecture/RESILIENCE_GUIDE.md)

## Full CLI, MCP and A2A > OmniRoute ships a command-line client with **91 top-level commands and command groups** (754 commands counting subcommands), an **MCP server with 110 tools and 33 scopes**, and an **A2A agent with 6 skills**. Scripts, terminals and AI agents can all operate the same gateway. ### A real CLI, not just `start` ```bash omniroute # start the gateway and dashboard (port 20128) omniroute setup # guided first-run wizard omniroute repl # interactive chat in the terminal (/model /combo /skill /memory) omniroute chat "hello" # one-shot prompt; also reads --file or --stdin omniroute doctor # check config, database, ports, Node runtime and native deps ``` The global `--output table|json|jsonl|csv` flag makes the same commands usable from scripts and CI. ### Remote mode: the CLI on your laptop, OmniRoute on a server Log in once to a remote server. The CLI saves it as a **context**, and later commands run against that server until you switch back. ```bash omniroute connect omniroute.example.com # asks for the password, saves a scoped token as a context omniroute models # runs against the remote server omniroute configure codex # picks a remote model, writes a local Codex profile omniroute tokens create --name ci --scope read # mint a narrower token for another machine omniroute contexts use default # switch back to the local server ``` | Token scope | What it allows | | ----------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- | | `read` | List and inspect: models, status, logs, usage | | `write` | `read` plus configure and apply: client setup, keys, config | | `admin` | `write` plus manage: tokens, providers, services, policy | A bare host gets `http://` and port 20128; pass a full `https://` URL when the server sits behind TLS. Routes that can spawn processes stay loopback-only, whatever the token. [Remote Mode guide](docs/guides/REMOTE-MODE.md)
### Connect an agent An agent, or your own code, can drive routing, providers, combos, cache, compression and memory through any of these interfaces. HTTP paths are served by the gateway, by default at `http://localhost:20128`. | Interface | Endpoint or command | Use it for | | ------------------------ | -------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | MCP over stdio | `omniroute --mcp` | Claude Desktop, Cursor and other local MCP clients | | MCP over Streamable HTTP | `/api/mcp/stream` | Remote MCP clients: 110 tools, 33 scopes, every call written to the audit log | | MCP over SSE | `/api/mcp/sse` | Clients that still use the SSE transport | | A2A discovery | `/.well-known/agent.json` | Agent Card: tells other agents what OmniRoute can do | | A2A execution | `POST /a2a` | JSON-RPC 2.0 tasks, synchronous or streamed over SSE, across 6 skills | | REST API | `/v1/*` | OpenAI-compatible chat, Responses, embeddings, images, audio and OCR | | Webhooks | `/api/webhooks` | Events to Slack, Discord, Telegram, or any URL with HMAC signing | | Remote CLI | `omniroute connect ` | Drive a remote instance with scoped access tokens | The six A2A skills are `smart-routing`, `quota-management`, `provider-discovery`, `cost-analysis`, `health-report` and `list-capabilities`. **Before you connect:** - **MCP over HTTP starts disabled.** Turn it on with `omniroute mcp enable --transport streamable-http` or from the dashboard's Endpoints page. One HTTP transport is active at a time: `streamable-http` serves `/api/mcp/stream`, `sse` serves `/api/mcp/sse`. - **A2A starts disabled.** Enable it on the dashboard's Endpoints page. `POST /a2a` then follows the same API-key rules as `/v1`. - **Remote MCP needs a suitable key.** `/api/mcp/*` answers only loopback by default. From another host, send a key with `manage` or `admin` (all tools), or with `mcp:connect` plus the scopes of the tools you need. ## Save 15–95% Tokens — Automatically ### How it works — pipeline, architecture & savings math Default stacked combo runs `RTK → Caveman`. When both act on the same tool/context payload, savings compound: ```txt combined = 1 − (1 − RTK) × (1 − Caveman_input) average = 1 − (1 − 0.80) × (1 − 0.46) = 89.2% range = 78.4 – 94.6% ``` Code blocks, URLs, JSON and structured data are **always protected** by the preservation engine. > **Why use many tokens when few tokens do the trick?** Every request passes through OmniRoute's compression pipeline **transparently** — no client changes. It's now a **stack of 12 composable engines** that run in order and mix & match per routing combo — building on ideas from [RTK](https://github.com/rtk-ai/rtk), [Caveman](https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman) (⭐ 90K+), [LLMLingua-2](https://github.com/microsoft/LLMLingua), and [Troglodita](https://github.com/leninejunior/troglodita) (PT-BR). ### The 12-engine stack Engines run in pipeline order; each is independently toggleable and configurable per combo:

12OmniGlyphExperimental context-as-image encoding for measured Claude Fable 5 on the direct Anthropic wire; GPT 5.6 transformers remain fail-closed pending provider receipts. Four compression profiles (aggressive default, balanced, coding-safe, passthrough) (most aggressive; opt-in)

Available for `zh`. | Each style has `lite`, `full` and `ultra` intensities. Add a style with an entry in the output style registry. #### Adaptive context budget | Setting | Options | | ------- | ------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- | | Policy | `reserve-output` (default) sets aside room for the reply and a safety margin. `percentage` uses a share of the context window. `absolute` sets a fixed token target. | | Mode | `floor` can escalate the selected plan to fit the context window. `replace-autotrigger` uses the budget for automatic escalation. `off` keeps the token-threshold auto-trigger. | #### Where compression is decided | Order | Source | | ----- | ------------------------------------------------------- | | 1 | Recognized `x-omniroute-compression` request header | | 2 | Routing combo override | | 3 | Active named profile | | 4 | Adaptive context budget or token-threshold auto-trigger | | 5 | Compression panel default | | 6 | Off when no plan applies | The global compression switch takes priority over this table. ## More install methods — Docker, source, pnpm, Arch **🐳 Docker** ```bash docker run -d --name omniroute --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 40 \ -p 127.0.0.1:20128:20128 -v omniroute-data:/app/data cheaperinference/omniroute:latest ``` `:latest` follows the highest **published** stable SemVer. It does not track git `main`. Pin `:X.Y.Z` for GitOps. See [Docker Release Channels](docs/guides/DOCKER_GUIDE.md#release-channels).The image pins **`OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=1024`**. That is enough for the dashboard and a light chat. **Coding agents** (`POST /v1/responses` from Claude Code, Codex, Grok, …) need a much larger V8 heap or the process `FATAL ERROR`s at ~12 GiB under two overlapping long contexts. Size the container above the heap (native buffers sit outside V8): | Workload | Heap (`-e OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB`) | Container (`--memory`) | | --------------------------------------------- | ------------------------------- | ---------------------- | | Dashboard / light chat | `1024` (image default) | ≥2 g | | One coding agent | `8192` | ≥10 g | | Two concurrent long `/v1/responses` | `10240`–`12288` | ≥12–16 g | ```bash docker run -d --name omniroute --restart unless-stopped --stop-timeout 40 \ -e OMNIROUTE_MEMORY_MB=8192 --memory=10g \ -p 127.0.0.1:20128:20128 -v omniroute-data:/app/data cheaperinference/omniroute:latest ``` Full table: [Docker Guide — runtime RAM](docs/guides/DOCKER_GUIDE.md#runtime-ram-for-coding-agents). > **Pre-release Docker channel:** `diegosouzapw/omniroute:next` and > `diegosouzapw/omniroute:next-web` follow the current default `release/v*` > branch. These mutable tags are intended only for testing unreleased fixes and > are **not supported for production**. See > [Docker Release Channels](docs/guides/DOCKER_GUIDE.md#release-channels). **🥟 Bun** Standard `bun install` and global installation (`bun install -g omniroute`) are supported via Bun runtime detection: - **Built-in `bun:sqlite`**: OmniRoute uses Bun's built-in `bun:sqlite` driver when running under Bun, falling back to `better-sqlite3` on Node.js or `sql.js`. - **Automatic Webpack bundler selection in dev**: Development (`bun run dev`) automatically detects Bun and disables Turbopack in favor of Webpack to prevent native V8 binding incompatibilities. Production builds (`bun run build`) follow `OMNIROUTE_USE_TURBOPACK` exactly as on Node: Turbopack by default, `OMNIROUTE_USE_TURBOPACK=0` to build with Webpack (`Dockerfile.bun` exposes it as a `--build-arg`). - **Dedicated Bun Dockerfile**: Multi-stage `Dockerfile.bun` for native Bun production deployments (`docker build -f Dockerfile.bun -t omniroute:bun .`). ```bash # Install and run with Bun bun install bun run dev ``` **🛠️ From source** ```bash cp .env.example .env && npm install PORT=20128 npm run dev ``` **📦 pnpm** ```bash pnpm add -g omniroute@latest --allow-build=better-sqlite3 --allow-build=@swc/core && omniroute ``` **🐧 Arch Linux (AUR)** ```bash yay -S omniroute-bin && systemctl --user enable --now omniroute.service ``` **🔧 Nix (Flake)** ```bash # Using Nix flakes nix develop npm run dev # Or using devbox devbox run npm run dev ``` 📖 [Docker Guide](docs/guides/DOCKER_GUIDE.md) — Compose profiles, Caddy HTTPS, Cloudflare tunnels. **🦭 Podman** ```bash # 1. Prepare the bind-mounted data directory mkdir -p data # 2. Linux + local rootless Podman only (never a remote Podman Machine client): podman unshare chown 1000:1000 ./data # 3. Set the runtime hint, build the local Compose image, and start echo "CONTAINER_HOST=podman" >> .env podman compose --profile base up -d --build ``` On macOS or Windows, Podman uses a remote Podman Machine: skip `podman unshare` and follow the [topology-specific data directory guidance](contrib/podman/README.md#data-directory-permissions-by-topology). 📖 [Podman Guide](contrib/podman/README.md) — Compose builds, Podman Machine, and Linux/systemd Quadlet setup. **⚡ Faster / leaner install (skip the native build)** The native SQLite engine (`better-sqlite3`) is an **optional** dependency, so a global install never blocks on compiling from source: it uses a prebuilt binary when one matches your platform/Node, and otherwise falls back transparently to a pure-JS engine (`node:sqlite` on Node 22+, else the bundled `sql.js` WASM) — no build tools required. To skip the post-install **native warm-up** entirely (CI, headless, or slow machines). Note: this only skips the native SQLite warm-up step (`scripts/postinstall.mjs`); the binary-copy/repair hook (`scripts/build/postinstall.mjs`) still runs normally: ```bash OMNIROUTE_SKIP_POSTINSTALL=1 npm install -g omniroute # CI=1 also skips it ``` For the fastest installs prefer **pnpm** (content-addressed store + hard links — see above). For a dashboard-free, headless runtime use the Docker `base` profile (above) or the [Termux guide](docs/guides/TERMUX_GUIDE.md). The CLI and the web dashboard are served by the same process on one port, so there is no separate CLI-only package today.
